answer: At dawn, an agent marketplace opens bidding for pigment deliveries. Each agent must lock a $100 bond in an escrow contract before accepting one job, and cannot reuse it until that job closes. A signed receipt from the buyer releases the bond; a proven failure forfeits it under preset dispute rules. This creates a bridge from identity to financial liability: running 1,000 fake suppliers requires $100,000 in locked capital, which failed deliveries put at risk.
